svg.text: Attachment: the one thing that fixes most feeding problems
Sore nipples, a hungry baby and a mother convinced she has no milk usually share a single cause.
Good attachment — four signs
More areola visible above the top lip
than below the bottom one
Mouth wide open
Lower lip turned outwards
Chin touching the breast
Slow deep sucks with pauses to swallow.
Rapid shallow sucking means she has the nipple only.
What poor attachment causes
Cracked, painful nipples
Engorgement, then mastitis
A baby who feeds constantly and
still does not gain weight
A mother told she has "weak milk"
She stops, and buys formula she
cannot afford or prepare safely.
How to know the baby is getting enough
Six or more wet nappies a day · steady weight gain after the first week · settled and alert between feeds ·
audible swallowing during the feed.
A crying baby is not evidence of too little milk, and a soft breast is not evidence of an empty one.
What the nurse should do before advising anything else
Watch a whole feed. Almost every question about milk supply, pain or weight is answered by seeing how the baby
is attached, and most of them are corrected by repositioning her at the breast rather than by adding anything.
